name: Visual Science
notes: Five courses. NEEDS VERIFICATION: the department page specifies only two of the five (one foundation course and one upper-level course) and does not say what the other three are. The third group below is the planner's placeholder for them - confirm with the Center for Visual Science before relying on it.
There is NO minor in neuroscience; neuroscience courses may be used as electives toward either the BCS minor or the biology minor.
CVSC 111, CVSC 153, CVSC 504 and CVSC 505 are absent from the 2025-26 catalog under those codes; their BCSC cross-listings are used where the catalog has them.

requirementGroups.label: One foundation course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Minor in Visual Science. Five courses are required. One of the following: CVSC/BCSC 110: Neural Foundations of Behavior; CVSC/BCSC 111: Foundations of Cognitive Science; CVSC/BCSC 153: Cognition; BCSC 240/NSCI 201: Basic Neurobiology; CVSC/BCSC 151: Perception & Action; OPT 248/448: Vision and the Eye
requirementGroups.note: Each of these is cross-listed under both CVSC and BCSC; either code counts. The catalog carries CVSC 110, CVSC 151, and the BCSC forms of the rest.

requirementGroups.label: One upper-level visual-science course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following upper-level courses: CVSC/BCSC 220: The Intelligent Eye; CVSC/BCSC 245: Sensory & Motor Neuroscience; CVSC/BCSC 504: Sensory Systems (with permission of instructor); CVSC/BCSC 505: Perception & Motor Systems (with permission of instructor); CVSC/BCSC 391: Independent Study (one semester only)
requirementGroups.note: CVSC 504 and 505 need the instructor's permission; CVSC/BCSC 391 counts for one semester only.

requirementGroups.label: Three further visual-science courses
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the page names only the two required categories above and states a five-course total without listing what the other three should be. Confirm the remaining three with the Center for Visual Science.
